newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Democrats lays off controversial fundraiser.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Democrats lays off controversial fundraiser.

text.p: The Democratic National Committee has laid off fundraiser John Huang, who solicited several controversial campaign contributions from foreign interests, a party spokeswoman said on Monday.
Amy Weiss Tobe said Huang was among 50 DNC employees laid off on Friday as the election season wound down. She said the decision was not due to the controversy surrounding Huang.

"He was let go as part of the downsizing" at the committee after the Nov. 5 election, she said. Huang had already been relieved of his fundraising duties, but he continued to draw a salary from the party until last week.

Huang, a former Commerce Department official, had been the DNC's finance vice chairman since December 1995 and raised $2.5 million for the party, much of it from the Asian-American community. But nearly $600,000 of this has been returned after questions were raised about the source of the money.
This included $250,000 that came from a Korean company rather than its U.S. subsidiary. It is illegal for foreign nationals to contribute to U.S. elections.

Questions about Democratic fundraising were an issue in the closing weeks of the presidential campaign and some analysts believe the controversy reduced President Bill Clinton's margin of victory over Republican Bob Dole.

The contributions prompted Republicans to accuse foreign interests of seeking influence with the Democratic president, and spurred internal investigations by the Commerce Department and the DNC. Clinton has denied that he has been influenced by foreign donations.

Tobe said on Monday that the DNC was returning another $5,000 raised at fundraiser at a Buddhist temple in April, a venue the party now says was inappropriate for a fundraiser. She said it had been established that the woman who made the donation was not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
The DNC previously returned $5,000 after another woman at the temple fundraiser said she was given the cash in small bills and asked to make the donation.
